traps.why: You handed over the magnesium alkoxide. Add H₃O⁺ to protonate it to the alcohol.
Acid before the carbonyl partner just protonates the Grignard: you get the alkane and no new C–C bond. Partner first, then H₃O⁺.
That is only the product after step 1; it still needs 1. (CH₃)₂C=O; 2. H₃O⁺.
There is a reaction: 1. Mg, ether; 2. (CH₃)₂C=O; 3. H₃O⁺ does change bromoethane.

explanation: The Grignard adds to the ketone carbonyl; H₃O⁺ gives the 3° alcohol.

flaws.why: You handed over the magnesium alkoxide. Add H₃O⁺ to protonate it to the alcohol.
Step 1 ((CH₃)₂C=O) does nothing here: Make the Grignard first (Mg, dry ether), then add the carbonyl / epoxide partner.

distractors.name: bromobenzene
distractors.why: With 1. Mg, ether; 2. (CH₃)₂C=O; 3. H₃O⁺, bromobenzene gives a different product (shown).
